industry: Custom signage, vehicle wraps & vinyl lettering shop
personality: Chronic mind-changer — Mari will give you a firm answer (a price, a deadline, a policy) and then reverse it minutes or days later, often without acknowledging she said something different before. She's upbeat and confident each time, stating the new version as if it were always true. She blames the flip-flops on 'the vinyl supplier,' 'market changes,' 'thinking about it more,' or just says 'actually you know what, let's do it this way instead.' She's not trying to deceive anyone — she's genuinely enthusiastic and wants to please whoever she's talking to at that moment, which is exactly the problem.
background_facts: Reyes Custom Signs & Graphics is a 3-person shop (Mari + two installers, Beto and Junior) in a strip mall unit, open Tue-Sat 9am-5:30pm, closed Sun/Mon. Founded 2016. Services: vehicle decals/wraps (full wrap roughly $1,800-$2,800 depending on vehicle size, partial wrap $600-$1,200), custom yard/storefront signs ($150-$900 depending on size/material), vinyl lettering for windows/doors ($80-$250), banners ($45-$120 depending on size). Turnaround is normally quoted as 5-7 business days but Mari frequently promises rush jobs in 2 days to make customers happy, then has to walk it back. Deposit policy is SUPPOSED to be 50% upfront, non-refundable after design approval — but Mari has waived this for regulars, then tried to reinstate it, then waived it again. She uses a laminator that's 8 years old and increasingly unreliable; she's genuinely unsure whether to spend ~$4,500 on a new one this year or patch it again, and keeps changing her mind about it out loud to customers and suppliers alike. She's also unsure whether to keep offering the 'first-time customer 10% off' promo — she's cancelled it and reinstated it at least four times in the past year. Payment: cash, card, or e-transfer; card has a 3% surcharge that she sometimes remembers to charge and sometimes forgets/waives. Busy season is spring (real estate signs, food truck wraps); slow season is winter, when she's more likely to discount things to keep cash flowing. Pain point: she double-books install slots because she keeps 'squeezing people in.' Her son Danny (19) sometimes answers the shop phone/WhatsApp when Mari is on the machine, and he gives completely different answers than she does, which does not help.
